top_cited_works.title: A transfer-matrix approach for estimating the characteristic impedance and wave numbers of limp and rigid porous materials
top_cited_works.venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
top_cited_works.abstract: A method for evaluating the acoustical properties of homogeneous and isotropic porous materials that may be modeled as fluids having complex properties is described here. To implement the procedure, a conventional, two-microphone standing wave tube was modified to include: a new sample holder; a section downstream of the sample holder that accommodated a second pair of microphone holders and an approximately anechoic termination. Sound-pressure measurements at two upstream and two downstream locations were then used to estimate the two-by-two transfer matrix of porous material samples. The experimental transfer matrix method has been most widely used in the past to measure the acoustical properties of silencer system components. That procedure was made more efficient here by taking advantage of the reciprocal nature of sound transmission through homogeneous and isotropic porous layers. The transfer matrix of a homogeneous and isotropic, rigid or limp porous layer can easily be used to identify the material's characteristic impedance and wave number, from which other acoustical quantities of interest can be calculated. recent_works.title: Sound absorption of multiscale sorptive permeable media with a distribution of nanopores
recent_works.abstract: Multiscale porous materials have shown remarkable acoustic properties. Among them, activated carbons stand out due to the multitude of physical phenomena, including sorption in nanopores, that strongly influence and enhance their sound attenuating performance. In the present work, an upscaled multiple porosity model for wave propagation in activated carbons exhibiting a bimodal nanopore size distribution was derived by using the two-scale asymptotic method of homogenisation. This model incorporates the different physics of wave propagation in the materials' inter-granular voids, their inner-grain transport pores and in their different types of nanopores, as well. The theoretical results are numerically illustrated to highlight the impact of the nanopore size distribution, in particular. Further, model predictions based on material parameters, obtained from an inverse fitting routine informed by parameters measured with non-acoustic experimental techniques, have been successfully compared with measured acoustic properties. recent_works.title: A multi-microphone technique for extending the upper-frequency measurement range in an acoustic impedance tube
recent_works.abstract: High frequency extension methods have recently been gaining attention for measuring the sound absorption coefficient and transmission loss when using acoustic impedance tubes. The usual upper-frequency limit can be extended by approximately four times beyond the traditional two-microphone tube of the same diameter by suppressing the contributions of high frequency cross-sectional modes within the tube. In this study, Finite Element Method (FEM) simulation models were developed to compare circular and square-section tubes and distinct advantages of the square-section configuration were identified. In square-section tubes, all cross-modes are symmetrical and so can be easily canceled by simply summing the signals from flush-mounted microphones. In contrast, circular tubes feature radial modes that cannot be so easily canceled. To further explore the extension method, the effects of microphone placement and spacing were studied with simulated porous foams and micro-perforated plates as the test articles.
